versions.note: First version: the cell-and-scales lens and the engine lens
Input fixes after the real-input check; two capability claims reworded; second-provider conflicts drawn
Cell view redrawn after the README's biology map: flat cut, natural colours with status dots, labels on leader lines, schematic and to-scale size modes, scale bar
Data refreshed after merging main (reactions operator registered, D156's status levels, new in-design items); to-scale mitochondria drawn as clear curved membranes with their inner folds

Protein atlas added as the second of three views (Cell and scales, Protein atlas, Engine): the 49 functional units of the law inventory of 12 November 2026, linked to their engine parts and to the public atlases; secreted-species transport shown as numerically qualified in its stated scope

Experiments added as the third of four views, before Engine: three E07-v1 runs replayed (the inheritance route, fast k1 at s 1.0, seed 5, recorded as erosion; and the control at seed 1, s 0.6 recorded as neutral and s 1.0 as erosion), 0.45 to 0.75 MB each, published as files beside the page; the organism outline is a planarian and the organ its brain; the map gained the feature requests of 14 November as planned parts and five corrections from a review against main

The scales are nested again (the user: the planarian was just hanging there): the sheet lies on the worm's head above its brain, with slanted views, so zooming out leads from tissue into organ into organism

An experiment selector with what each experiment found as two facts from the record; 59 runs of two experiments (all 38 of E07-v1 and the 21-arm turnover pre-screen; 34.5 MB, largest 0.87 MB); the sheet stands for skin-like tissue over the brain, with the cell among its neighbours; the atlas counts 25 gained identifiers with a dated review; three feature requests shown as designed

The cell is drawn flat-sided, as a cell packed in the skin-like layer (the user: a bit more like a planarian skin cell): six sides with rounded corners, 13 µm tall like the sheet's cells, among six glass neighbours; what enters or leaves the cell sits at the corners. The map gained the operator species_regulated_availability@1 (milestone 1, development code) with its law and its references, the species cap at 16, excitable tissue accepted narrowly (D170) and the conduction probe's outcome. The atlas card says 28 identifiers gained, 25 of them reviewed. Built, checked (35 of 35) and exported from a clean checkout of the branch at 543bab87; the 59 run files are unchanged

Species atlases: a Species switch on the protein atlas (Human, Planarian). The planarian atlas of Schmidtea mediterranea has an entry for all 49 units: products of the same family found for 38, a different family for 3 (gap junctions from innexins), nothing found for 2, nothing to look for in 6; 204 gene products, 200 of them candidates by family signature. A ring marks a unit where the species differs. The library of about 10,000 planarian proteins was found and not imported. Checked with 55 of 55 real-input checks and 93 tests (92 pass, 1 skipped) at 54850de6; the page is 1.14 MB, and the 59 run files are unchanged

First version at the new link: the same page as the last version at the earlier link, with two corrections (the conduction probe shown as designed, since its driver has no test; the human atlas says its Xenopus entries are links only). The page and all 59 run files were published together (60 files, 35.7 MB). Tests and checks at 4ba6710c: 93 tests (92 pass, 1 skipped); the species and engine parts of the input check after the corrections, and all 55 checks before them

The map at main 6ae5b388: the scheduled bath is a registered operator (FR-10's first milestone, development code); the coupling operator's first two milestones are in; MG0c's protocol is revised and still proposed; the conduction probe's text says what was compared blind. The page is otherwise unchanged, and the 59 run files were not sent again. Checked at 3ce44705: 55 of 55 real-input checks on a clean checkout (one label check had failed once under heavy machine load and was made to wait for the label to hold still); 95 tests (94 pass, 1 skipped)

JCVI-syn3A is a third species in the protein atlas: none of the inventory's 49 units is found in it (43 nothing found, 6 nothing to look for), and nine of its own membrane machines are listed apart. The map shows the Syn3A minimal-cell track as planned (D173), the coupling operator's third milestone and the excitable-tissue references. An interim view: the species switch that also changes the levels and the shapes is still being built. Checked at 38866504 on a clean checkout: 55 of 55 real-input checks; 113 tests (112 pass, 1 skipped). The 59 run files were not sent again

Mycoplasma pneumoniae is a fourth species in the protein atlas: none of the inventory's 49 units is found in it, and nine of its own membrane machines are listed apart. The map shows the coupling operator's proposed qualification protocol, the composition matrix and the Syn3A track's revision. Still an interim view: the species switch that changes the levels and the shapes, and the shelves of each species' own proteins, are being built. Checked at 634ab261 on a clean checkout: 55 of 55 real-input checks; 146 tests (145 pass, 1 skipped). The 59 run files were not sent again

One species for the whole page (Human, Planarian, Syn3A, M. pneumoniae): the switch in the top bar sets the levels, the shapes, what the cell holds and the species' side of the protein atlas, all from data files. Syn3A and M. pneumoniae end at their cell; the human heart and body are rough placeholders. The map shows the coupling operator as numerically qualified and MG0c's protocol as registered. Checked at 4e89be16 on a clean checkout: 55 of 55 real-input checks, 38 of 38 species checks, 177 tests (176 pass, 1 skipped). The species' own proteins on shelves are not drawn yet. The 59 run files were not sent again

The species' facts now rest on permissively licensed sources only: every source in the data files is classed by licence, and no value comes from a non-commercial source or one with no stated terms (M. pneumoniae is drawn with 300 ribosomes, from an open paper's measurement). The map shows both the coupling operator and the reactions operator as numerically qualified (MG0c judged, 55 of 55). Checked on a clean checkout of the branch head: 55 of 55 real-input checks, 38 of 38 species checks, 185 tests (184 pass, 1 skipped). The 59 run files were not sent again

Each species' own proteins on shelves in the protein atlas, in one format: Syn3A's 455 and M. pneumoniae's 688 one marker each, the planarian's 18,882 as families that open; a switch on the card moves between Cells' 49 machines and the species' own proteins. 12 protein files (3.4 MB) are now published beside the page with the 59 runs: 72 files with the page. The map shows the cell-owned compartment and site-occupancy operators and the run-view design note. Checked at b760d062: 55 of 55 real-input checks, 41 of 41 species checks, shelves checks 17 of 17 (Syn3A), 18 of 18 (planarian) and 6 of 6 (without the files); 211 tests (210 pass, 1 skipped)

In the species' own proteins, what is inside the cell now stands in coloured glass like the membrane shelf, a little lighter; what is set apart keeps none. The map follows main through 44227075, and the atlas says that the catalogue's 34 added entries were reviewed (no channel, pump, transporter or junction law among them). Checked at aa4a3cbe: 55 of 55 real-input checks, 41 of 41 species checks, shelves checks 17 of 17 (Syn3A), 18 of 18 (planarian) and 6 of 6 (without the files); 211 tests (210 pass, 1 skipped). The 71 files beside the page were not sent again

The map gains the modular inner model (D172, D176: designed, in implementation on an integration branch, not on main) and levels of detail (D175), and says of the composite what the record says of the L4 (agreement within tolerance; the bitwise criterion open). Every 'qualified' label was checked against main's record at f791294c. Checked on a clean copy of 15549fd4: the scene built strictly with no warning; 211 tests (210 pass, 1 skipped); the engine's real-input checks, 4 of 4. Nothing else changed since Version 8, whose full checks stand; the 71 files beside the page were not sent again

The engine map level with main 1bd1cfbd after a pass over every entry: the modular rework of the inner model is a hub that delivers eleven designed parts, each saying what holds today and that it is not on main, and the Cell view says part by part what runs today and what the rework brings (designed 10 to 24, qualified 39 to 40). In the species' own proteins every tool behind a predicted placement is named with its own terms and counts, and Syn3A's lipid anchors come from a sequence rule of the tool's own (5 proteins outside where 13 were), pending the user's decision on values a restricted tool computed. Checked on a clean copy: 55 of 55 real-input checks and 41 of 41 species checks at e6396b3a, shelves checks 17 of 17 (Syn3A), 18 of 18 (planarian) and 6 of 6 (without the files) at b210a54a, where only the check itself differs; 226 tests (225 pass, 1 skipped). Sent with the page: the three species' shelves files; the other 68 files beside it are unchanged

Versions 11 and 12, one build sent in two uploads (the page with the species' proteins; then the replays). New: the first quantity layers on replays (voltage relief; junction drops; a quiet and a bold strength; a panel that says what stands behind a layer), each replay with a file for its junctions; the species selection as a dropdown; the human's own proteins on six stacked shelves (20,414); E. coli as a fifth species with its 4,403 proteins on two shelves; the engineered protein cage left out of the Cell view and the atlas (48 machines drawn of the inventory's 49); Syn3A's lipid anchors from UniProt again (13 proteins outside), with every tool behind a placement named and counted under the user's rule. Built from a clean copy of 1326ebbc. Real-click checks there: input 55 of 55, species 58 of 58, shelves Syn3A 17 of 17, planarian 18 of 18 (on a second run with the browser quiet; 16 of 18 on the first, a click sent while the view still moved), without files 6 of 6, layer zero 6 of 6, the layers' switch 14 of 14 once the check waits for the bar's label (13 of 14 as committed there). The human scenario gave 24 of 25 in each of three runs here, on two different steps, and 25 of 25 in the agent's own run: taken as the check pressing before the view has settled on a busy machine, not as a fault of the page; its pictures show the stack and every shelf's name as intended. 146 files beside the page (55 MB). Not in this build, though on the branch: the fruit fly, E. coli's chemotaxis set in 'show by', the close-up of a chosen cell, E. coli's appendages as data; thale cress is held back

Versions 13 and 14, one build sent in two uploads (the page with the fruit fly's proteins and half of the replays; then the rest of the replays). New: the fruit fly as a sixth species, with its 13,814 proteins (one for each gene) on six stacked shelves; the Cell view's resting look (studio reflections, filmic light, soft translucency, contact shade, surface texture, a drift of the crowd, a shimmer on the membrane) with a Look switch back to the plain picture; on a replay, the close-up of a chosen cell's membrane, with the push and pull on each ion and the membrane's charge, and each replay with files for its ions' concentrations; E. coli's 'Show by', with its chemotaxis proteins and the assemblies a protein is part of. Built from a clean copy of 9ae6f867. Real-click checks there: species 60 of 60; shelves Syn3A 17 of 17, planarian 18 of 18, without files 6 of 6, human 25 of 25, E. coli 5 of 5; layers zero 7 of 7, the switch 14 of 14, the close-up 19 of 19; the look 21 of 21, its switch 19 of 19, the other views 12 of 12; input 54 of 55. The one miss was the check's own: it read a label's place while the camera still glided, with the look drawn slowly in software. With the check waiting for drawn frames and a still camera, the Cell view's part gave 11 of 11 twice, the look on. Six pictures of the build were looked at (the cell of the planarian and of the fruit fly, the fruit fly's and E. coli's proteins, a replay in the dark theme, the cell on a phone). 331 files beside the page (109 MB), of which the 244 that changed were sent. Known flaw: on a phone the look's note, the scale bar and the caveat overlap at the foot of the Cell view. Not in this build, though on the branch: quantity layers stage 3 (transfers, ion traffic, energy dissipated, the secreted species; the engine's development run and the marked example); the scene at main 2c00d08d. Flagella, pili and a plant cell's parts are drawn and not yet committed; thale cress is held back

Version 15, one upload. New: thale cress as a seventh species, under a third heading (Plants), with a plant cell (a wall, a large vacuole, chloroplasts, a four-sided cell and a sheet packed in squares, said to be the picture's choice) and its 27,368 proteins on nine shelves; E. coli's flagella and pili, drawn from its file, with the foot of a flagellum opening the Protein atlas on the 34 proteins of its flagellum; quantity layers stage 3 on replays: transfers as beads across borders (one bead a stated number of molecules, at true speed with a slow-down), ion traffic through a chosen cell's channels, pump and membrane, the rate of each dissipated-energy ledger as a glow, and the secreted species as a fog; the engine's first development run for the viewer (one cell that secretes a species) under 'Development run', and an example with invented numbers under 'Example', marked on the picture and in the legend; an example's card without the tick of a finished run; the scene at main 2c00d08d. Built from a clean copy of d713144b. Real-click checks there, one run each: input 55 of 55; species 62 of 62; shelves Syn3A 17 of 17, planarian 18 of 18, without files 6 of 6, human 25 of 25, E. coli 5 of 5; layers zero 7 of 7, the switch 14 of 14, the close-up 19 of 19, flow 22 of 22 (held to numbers worked out from the run's own 64-bit arrays), the example 8 of 8; the look 21 of 21, the other views 12 of 12; the Cell view's part on E. coli 10 of 10 and on thale cress 11 of 11. The look's switch gave 18 of 19 in seven of nine runs, on the same line each time: in its window of 1040 by 640, where the page's own font had not arrived, the legend grew tall enough to lie over the view's card, so the press on 'Status' fell on the legend (seen in the page itself). That is a flaw of the page in a short window, older than this build, and not of the look; the run that waits for the font gave 19 of 19, as did one of the plain runs. The fix (the legend scrolls within the room left under the card) is on the branch and not in this build. Pictures looked at: the development run light, dark and on a phone, the example's close-up, the cell of thale cress and of E. coli, thale cress's proteins. 378 files beside the page (115 MB), of which the 47 that changed were sent. Known limits: on a phone the run's card covers part of a small world's picture; with the panel open the statement on a replay starts under the legend. Not in this build, though on the branch: flux in the Cell view (stage 4), built and not yet seen in a browser

Version 16, the page alone (no file beside it changed). New: flux in the Cell view, stage 4 of the quantity layers: a Flux switch in the legend, off as the page opens; a part's flux shows when the visitor chooses the part, and the switch shows all of it; beads with bloom, the look's own motion held still while they show. No species has a looping run of its own yet, so what shows is illustration of the form 'direction only', with 'Illustration: not a run' on the picture, in the legend and in the chosen part's panel: pumps go the way the engine's own laws say (3 sodium out and 2 potassium in; 1 calcium out), drawn for the species the page shows as the generic cell; secreted signals by the exchange operator's export and import; channels, junctions and water both ways with none claimed; fuel draws nothing, with the reason. A part named in the page's address shows no flux as the page opens. At rest the cell's water drops, signals and close-up ions now stand still: they moved with a direction and had no rate behind them. Also new: the legend no longer lies over the view's card in a short window (it scrolls within the room left under the card); on a replay the statement starts clear of the legend when a panel is open, and the beads keep true time whatever the gap between frames. Built from a clean copy of ae914a2a. Real-click checks there, one run each, all passed: input 55 of 55; species 62 of 62; shelves Syn3A 17, planarian 18, without files 6, human 25, E. coli 5, and thale cress's nine shelves 5 of 5; layers zero 7, the switch 14, the close-up 19, flow 22, the example 8; the look 21, its switch 19 (with the stand-in font, where it had missed before the legend's fix), the other views 12; flux in the Cell view 26 of 26 in light, dark, at 1040 by 640, moving, on thale cress and on E. coli, 24 of 24 on a phone, and the address 5 of 5; the Cell view's part on E. coli 12 of 12, with a real press on the door from a flagellum's foot into the Protein atlas (its flagellum's proteins picked out), and on thale cress 11 of 11. Each check but the flux check now says whether the page's own font had arrived; it had not in five of the runs (thale cress's shelves, the look's three, the Cell view's part on E. coli), which passed all the same. Pictures looked at, from this build: flux on E. coli, on thale cress, in the short window, on a phone, with a part chosen and by the address; in the dark, from the layers agent's copy. 378 files beside the page (115 MB), none sent. Known limits: at 400 px the Flux switch is reachable only with no panel open; a chosen part that draws nothing, and a run's longer statement on a phone, have not been seen in a browser; with a panel open the scale bar's words can touch the caveat

Versions 1 to 3 at the new link, one build sent in three uploads: the same build as Version 16 at the earlier link, byte for byte from the folder staged for it (out/publish-v16). Nothing was rebuilt and no check was run again: its checks are Version 16's, in the entry before this one. The page and all 378 files beside it were sent (115 MB): 134 files with the page, then 195, then 49. The link's own listing afterwards showed 379 files, and five of them compared by size with the ones on disk. The page was not looked at in a browser at the new link. Version numbers start again here: the next publish is this link's Version 4. Not in this build, though on the branch: a replay's own clock with slower and faster speeds, the cell's own motion back at rest, the pump's lanes in the membrane's close-up, green chloroplasts, and the engine map of 16 November 2026

Version 4 at the new link, the page alone (none of the 378 files beside it changed). New: the nucleus, the Golgi apparatus and the ribosomes are parts of the map of their own, planned and illustration only, by the user's decision of 16 November 2026 (docs/CELL_STRUCTURES.md): nothing of them is in the engine and each panel says so; 'Regulatory circuits' is drawn at the cell's DNA, and 'Membrane trafficking' at the vesicles; where colour shows the kind of part every part is drawn whole, and 'Colour: Status' shows what is not built as grey sketches; a structure the cell does not hold is read from the species' file, and a structure has a door into the Protein atlas where the species' own proteins can show its set. A replay's beads keep the replay's own clock: paused they stand; the timeline's speed lists steps from a million times slower to 240 times faster, each in words, and a replay keeps the speed it states on a slow device. In the Cell view the cell's own drops, signals and close-up ions move again at rest, and the legend says that this motion is the picture's own. Drawn to scale, the membrane's close-up has lanes over its pump. The veil over a shelf covers the whole shelf, seen at a slant. Chloroplasts are green where colour shows the kind of part. The engine map is that of 16 November 2026 (D183 on the living-cell loops and the excitable-tissue laws), stamped main fe0ca3ab. Built from a clean copy of 5830bfdf and published after main had the note the new parts cite (main 9a15108e). Checks on that content: the strict build clean; npm test exit 0, 445 tests, 444 pass, 1 skipped; every real-click scenario once, four at a time: 29 of 31 passed, 526 of 532 checks, in 21.9 minutes while other jobs shared the processors; the two that missed (the planarian's shelves and the layers' switch, both timing waits) passed alone three times of three, 18 of 18 and 14 of 14; the Cell view's input on the planarian, E. coli and thale cress again after a check was hardened, 13 of 13 each. Pictures looked at, from that content: the cell, the Golgi and the nucleus close, in light and dark, at 1440 by 900 with the stand-in font; the replay's speed list on a phone and in a short window. Not looked at in a browser at the published link by the session; the user looked at the link's Version 3 and said it works. Known limits: no colour check stands in the tests (the Golgi's pink was measured by hand against the other colours); on a phone the Flux switch is still reachable only with no panel open, and the other small-window limits of Version 16 stand (a polish pass is in hand); E. coli's wall is still drawn outside its outer membrane in this build (fixed on the branch after it). Not in this build: the flagellar motor's closer view, flux at real-life speed with a slow-down, the Laws library

versions.note: First version: six ways to draw flux, the options for time, for switching it on and for the source of its numbers (first the engine's looping run of each species' cell), ten resting-look effects that switch on and off, what devices offer, and the choices put to the user. Its pictures were checked as stills drawn in software; the sketches were not watched moving and no frame rate was measured there
